title: Onboarding observable snapshots playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose
This is a working draft for a lightweight playbook that standardizes the observable snapshot model we collect and present during customer-managed onboarding for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to give both Redwood operators and the customer a concise, tamper-resistant snapshot that proves a safe, auditable handoff without shipping huge volumes of telemetry.

Why this exists (problem statement)
- Customers onboarding Private deployments ask: did the customer-side config actually connect, did the handoff complete, and can we reproduce the exact state for post-mortem or compliance review?
- Current audit trails are either too noisy (full packet logs) or too sparse (only high-level events). We need a middle ground: small, verifiable evidence bundles that can be stored, sampled, and replayed.

Goals
- Define a minimal snapshot schema for onboarding events and periodic sampling.
- Provide an operator and customer view: concise human-readable summary + machine-readable capsule for replay.
- Ensure snapshots are encrypted in-transit and at-rest with customer-controlled keys where requested.
- Keep agent footprint <2MB and CPU <2% on an edge VM.

Non-goals
- This doc does not define full long-term forensic archives (that is a separate retention/forensics PRD).
- Not attempting to replicate full packet captures or deep-packet inspection.

Observable snapshot (high level)
Each snapshot = one compressed evidence capsule containing:
- capsule-metadata.txt (who, when, context)
- control-plane-events.jsonl (ordered events: connect, handshake, approval decisions, route binding)
- agent-heartbeat.log (sequence of short health pings with counters)
- net-sanity-checks.txt (results of scoped connectivity checks e.g. TLS handshake fingerprints, route checks)
- minimal topology map (peers, IPs, ASNs if available)
- config-diff.patch (what changed from last applied config, if any)
- verification-manifest.sha256 (hash list of files inside capsule)
- optional: cryptographic-proof.sig (if customer requests signature with their KMS key)

Design choices and rationale
- JSONL for events makes partial parsing and streaming possible. Avoid large monolithic JSON.
- Keep capsule size target < 100KB for typical onboarding to allow fast upload/storage.
- Use semantic names for events (e.g., CP_CONNECT, CP_BIND_ROUTE, APPROVAL_GRANTED) rather than raw logs to ease operator reading.
- Provide both a human summary and full capsule for investigators.

Sampling and retention tiers
- onboarding-full: capture every onboarding snapshot until the first successful handoff (default 30 days).
- post-onboard-sample: sample 1 in N daily heartbeats and record snapshot capsules weekly for first 90 days.
- compliance-hold: customer can request hold -> preserve last 365 days of capsules for that tenant.
- automatic purge: after retention elapses, capsules are deleted; deletion is itself recorded in the control-plane audit.

Approval gate UX and operator flow
- When a customer requests a VPC handoff, Redwood operator triggers Verify-on-Connect. The UI shows: summary card (connectivity ok/partial/fail), last capsule timestamp, sample artifacts available for download.
- If summary shows partial, operator can open the capsule replay view which replays ordered control-plane-events and indicates which check failed.
- Approval decision is recorded as an event (APPROVAL_GRANTED or APPROVAL_BLOCKED) and included in the next capsule.

Reproducible replay harness
- Minimal local tool (redwood-replay) that consumes a capsule and replays ordered events against a sandbox harness to reproduce observed sequence. Intended for SRE debugging and customer walk-throughs.
- The harness will not automatically perform destructive actions; it is read-only by default and requires explicit flags to simulate state changes.

Security & keying model
- Default: capsule encrypted with Redwood-managed envelope keys.
- Enterprise option: customer-supplied KMS key (bring-your-own-key) to encrypt capsules at rest. Redwood still records capsule metadata but cannot decrypt without customer consent.
- All capsules include a signature over the manifest to prove integrity. Signature key rotation must be logged as an event.

Privacy and PII minimization
- Strip payloads that include user content. Snapshot should not contain sample data from customer traffic; only control-plane and connectivity metadata.
- Net-sanity-checks avoid including full IP payloads. If IPs are sensitive for a customer, provide IP redaction option on the agent.

Agent implementation notes (rough)
- Language: Go micro-agent to minimize runtime deps.
- Behaviour: collect event stream, perform scoped connectivity checks (TLS handshake to control plane, port checks), compute diffs, assemble capsule, sign, upload to Redwood control plane endpoint.
- Resource cap: default limits CPU 2%, RAM 64MB, disk ephemeral <10MB.
- Config flags: --capsule-interval, --capsule-mode={onboard,periodic,sample}, --redwood-endpoint, --customer-kms-key.

Operator playbook for common scenarios
- Handshake fails: open capsule -> inspect CP_CONNECT events -> check TLS fingerprint mismatch -> common fixes: wrong CA, MTU path issue, customer firewall.
- Route bind timeout: inspect bind events and agent logs included in capsule; escalate to network team with capsule id.
- Approval disagreement: if customer and Redwood disagree, export capsule and run local redwood-replay together during call.

Metrics to evaluate rollout
- time-to-first-successful-capsule (median)
- capsule-size (p50/p95)
- onboarding-resolution-time post-capsule (how much faster ops resolve issues with capsule available)
- percentage of handoffs that needed replay assistance

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: local prototype + replay harness (engineering only).
- Phase 1: small alpha with 5 customers, manual review and feedback loop.
- Phase 2: gated beta with UI integration in Console and limited retention.
- Phase 3: general availability with BYOK and configurable retention tiers.

Open questions / risks
- Is 100KB capsule target realistic for some enterprise topologies? Need sampling data.
- Legal/regulatory: do any regions require different storage locations or additional redaction? Work with legal.
- Customer keys: how to implement key escrow or emergency decrypt?

Next steps (TODOs)
- [ ] Spike: implement Go agent prototype and measure capsule sizes for 10 different customer onboards (JIRA: PDP-789).
- [ ] UX: design console card and download flow (Design owner: Evelyn).
- [ ] SRE: draft redwood-replay tool spec and runbook (Assignee: Jonah).
- [ ] Legal: review retention tiers and export controls (Assignee: Roberto).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight — aim is to make onboarding evidence consumable by humans and machines quickly. Please push back if we are missing a compliance/regulatory requirement or if the capsule format feels too constrained for realistic on-prem customers.
- If you want different event names or a richer manifest, comment inline or add to linked JIRA PDP-789.

References
- Confluence: onboarding observability primer (linked in linked_artifacts)
- Jira: PDP-789 (prototype + alpha)
- GitHub: private-onboard-agent prototype PR (linked in linked_artifacts)
